stages.title: What doctors and healthcare workers do
stages.hook: Who helps you when you have a sore throat, a broken arm or a tooth that hurts? Are they all the same helper?
explain: Doctors help people who are ill or hurt. They listen, look, and ask questions. Then they work out what is wrong and how to help.
A doctor does not work alone. Nurses care for patients and watch over them. Pharmacists know all about medicines. Dentists look after teeth. Many helpers make a team.
Good helpers are kind and honest. If they are not sure, they ask another helper. That is a clever and safe thing to do.
This is a game. All the patients are made up. If you feel ill in real life, tell a grown-up.

example.q: Mia has a toothache. Who can help her best?
steps: The pain is in a tooth.
Dentists look after teeth.
So Mia should see a dentist.

analogies.home: A family helps each other at home. Healthcare helpers help each other too.
analogies.sport: A football team has a goalkeeper and players. A health team has doctors, nurses and more.
analogies.city: A town has bakers, drivers and builders. It also has health helpers for people who are ill.
analogies.farm: A vet cares for sick animals. A doctor cares for sick people.

stages.title: Human body parts
stages.hook: Can you point to your elbow, your knee and your chin? Which part of you helps you see, and which helps you hear?
explain: Your body has many parts. Your head has eyes to see, ears to hear, a nose to smell and a mouth to taste and speak.
Arms and legs help you move. Hands can hold things. Feet help you stand and walk. Elbows and knees are joints. They bend.
Doctors use the right names for body parts. Then everyone knows what part is meant.

stages.title: Basic body organs
stages.hook: Put your hand on your chest. What can you feel going thump, thump? What is inside making it happen?
explain: Inside you are parts called organs. Each organ has a big job. The heart pumps blood round your body. You can feel it beat.
The lungs are two soft bags in your chest. They take in air when you breathe. The air has oxygen that your body needs.
The brain is in your head. It helps you think, feel and move. The stomach mixes up food. The skin covers the outside and keeps you safe.

steps: Think about the thump in your chest.
That is the heart.
The heart pumps blood.

stages.title: Healthy eating
stages.hook: If a car needs fuel, what does your body need? Which foods give you power to play?
explain: Food is fuel for your body. It gives you energy to move and learn. It also helps you grow and mend.
Fruits and vegetables, grains like rice or bread or maize, beans, fish, eggs and milk are all good foods. Different places have different favourite foods, and many are healthy.
A mix is best. Sweets and sugary drinks are fine as a small treat, but not all day. Water is a great drink. Always tell a grown-up if you have an allergy to a food.

stages.title: Exercise and physical wellbeing
stages.hook: When you run, your heart beats fast. Is that a bad thing? What does moving do for your body?
explain: Moving your body is called exercise. Running, dancing, swimming, cycling and playing games are all exercise.
Exercise makes your heart, lungs, bones and muscles stronger. It also helps you feel happy and sleep well.
Rest is important too. Your body mends and grows when you sleep. Children need lots of sleep. Drink water when you play, and stop and tell a grown-up if you feel pain or feel dizzy.

example.q: Zara plays football for an hour. Her heart beats fast. Is this normal?
steps: Playing is hard work for muscles.

stages.title: Personal hygiene
stages.hook: You cannot see germs. So how do soap and water get rid of them?
explain: Hygiene means keeping yourself clean so you stay well. Washing your hands is the most important habit.
Wash your hands with soap and clean water after the toilet, before eating and after playing outside. Rub for as long as it takes to sing a song twice. Rinse and dry.
Brush your teeth every day. Have a bath or wash often. Cover your mouth when you cough, using your elbow or a tissue. Use clean water to drink.

stages.title: Germs and infection prevention
stages.hook: One child sneezes and soon three more feel ill. How did the germs jump from one to another?
explain: Germs are tiny living things. Some can make us ill. When germs get into the body and make us ill, it is called an infection. Not all germs are bad. Many are harmless and some are helpful.
Germs can spread through coughs and sneezes, dirty hands, dirty water and sharing cups. They can also spread by touching a surface and then your face.
We can stop them. Wash hands, cover coughs, stay home when ill, drink clean water and keep food clean. Vaccines are given by doctors and nurses and they help protect us from some serious illnesses.

example.q: Ben has a cough. How can he stop germs spreading to friends?
steps: Coughs push germs into the air.
Cover the cough with an elbow or a tissue.
Wash hands and rest at home if ill.
example.a: Cover his cough, wash his hands and rest at home

stages.title: Basic safety and recognising emergencies
stages.hook: If a friend is badly hurt and does not wake up, what should you do first? Who do you call?
explain: An emergency is when someone is badly hurt or very ill and needs help now. For example, someone is not breathing, there is a lot of blood, a fire, or a person cannot wake up.

If there is an emergency, stay as safe as you can and get a grown-up. Know the number to call for help in your country. Many places have one emergency number. Ask a grown-up what it is where you live.

Tell the helper where you are and what happened, in a calm voice. Do not hang up until they say. Staying safe also means looking before crossing roads, wearing helmets and never touching medicines unless a grown-up gives them.

example.q: You see smoke in the kitchen. What do you do?
steps: Smoke means fire may be near.
Do not try to fight it.
Get out, tell a grown-up and call for help.
example.a: Get out safely and tell a grown-up to call emergency help

A special vehicle that takes ill or hurt people to hospital.
The phone number you call for urgent help.

misc.right: Children should get a grown-up and call for help. Their job is to stay safe and ask for help.

stages.limits: Emergency numbers are different in different countries. Always ask a trusted adult what the number is where you live. This game is not a first-aid course. The people in it are made up.

trip.prompt: Find out that many countries have different emergency numbers.

questions.q: Which is an emergency?
o: A person who cannot wake up
A sleepy cat on the sofa all day
questions.why: Not waking up needs help now.

questions.q: You see a fire. What should you do?
o: Get out and tell a grown-up
Hide in a cupboard and wait
Stay and watch it grow bigger
questions.why: Get to safety and get help.

questions.q: Who takes ill people to hospital?
questions.why: Ambulances take people to hospital fast.

questions.q: A friend falls and is very hurt. What do you do first?
questions.why: Getting an adult quickly gets help.

questions.q: When you call for help, what should you say?
o: Where you are and what happened
A joke to cheer them up
questions.why: Helpers need to know where to go and what is wrong.

questions.q: You find some tablets on the floor. What do you do?
o: Do not touch them and tell a grown-up
Eat one to see what it is
Taste a tiny bit to see if it is sweet
questions.why: Medicines can be dangerous for children.

questions.q: Why should you look both ways before crossing a road?
o: To check no vehicle is coming
To count the cars and wave to them
questions.why: Looking keeps you safe from traffic.

questions.q: Match the problem to the best action.
pairs: Get out and call for help
Do not touch and tell an adult
questions.why: Each danger needs a safe, quick response.

questions.q: Should every country use the same emergency number?
o: No, ask a grown-up what yours is
questions.why: Numbers differ by place.

questions.q: Why stay calm when you call for help?
o: So the helper can understand you
So you can go to sleep
So you can win a prize for being quiet
questions.why: Calm and clear speech helps helpers act quickly.

panel.q: A small cut that stops bleeding and a person who cannot breathe. Which is an emergency?
o: The small cut that stopped bleeding
panel.why: Not breathing is life threatening. A small cut can be cleaned and covered.

panel.q: Why should a child not try to be a hero in a fire?
o: Getting out and calling help is safer
Heroes always win in the end
Adults are not needed at all in a fire
panel.why: Safety first, and get help.

panel.q: What should you do if you think someone has an emergency?
panel.model: Stay safe, get a grown-up quickly and call the emergency number to get help.
panel.why: Get an adult and call for help.

teach.topic: What to do in an emergency
teach.model: An emergency is when someone needs help right now. Stay safe, get a grown-up and call the emergency number. Tell them where you are and what happened.

points.ask: How do I ask for help?

stages.title: Understanding illness and recovery
stages.hook: When you have a cold you feel poorly, then slowly better. What is your body doing while you rest?
explain: Illness means the body is not working as it should. You may feel hot, tired, sore or sick. These feelings are called symptoms.
Your body fights illness. Rest, water and sometimes medicine from a doctor help. Most colds get better by themselves in a few days.
Tell a grown-up when you feel ill. If you feel very bad, are struggling to breathe, or do not get better, a doctor should check. Never take medicine unless a grown-up who knows gives it.

example.q: Lina has a sore throat and feels tired. What should she do?
steps: Tell a grown-up.
Rest and drink water.
If she gets worse, see a doctor.
example.a: Tell a grown-up, rest and drink water, and see a doctor if worse

analogies.home: When a phone battery is low it needs charging. When you are ill you need rest.
analogies.nature: A plant droops without water and then recovers. Bodies recover with care.
analogies.farm: A farmer rests a lame horse until it heals.
analogies.sport: A footballer who is hurt rests so the leg can mend.

stages.mnemonic: Tell, rest, drink, check: four steps to get better.
terms: A feeling that tells you something is wrong, like a sore throat.
When the body is hotter than normal.
Something a doctor or pharmacist gives to help you get better.

misc.wrong: Medicine is like sweets, so you can take it whenever you like.
misc.right: Medicine is strong. Only take it when a trusted grown-up gives it to you.

stages.limits: These are simple ideas with made-up patients. They are not advice for any real child.

trip.prompt: Find what helps people feel better when they have a cold.

questions.q: What is a symptom?
o: A feeling that shows you are ill
A kind of toy for the playground
A tall tree in the garden
questions.why: Symptoms tell us that something is wrong.

questions.q: You feel ill. What should you do first?
questions.why: A grown-up can help or call a doctor.

questions.q: What helps your body recover from a cold?
questions.why: Rest and water help the body fight.

questions.q: Who should give you medicine?
o: Nobody and you take it yourself
questions.why: Medicine can be unsafe if used wrongly.

questions.q: Which sign needs help right away?
questions.why: Struggling to breathe is an emergency.

questions.q: What does recovery mean?
questions.why: Recovery is getting better.

questions.q: Put these in order for a child with a sore throat.
items: See a doctor if not getting better
questions.why: First tell an adult, rest, and see a doctor if it does not improve.

questions.q: Why do we stay home from school when we have a fever?
o: To rest and not spread germs
Because school is closed for the day
To watch the clouds drift by
questions.why: Rest helps us recover and others stay well.

questions.q: Pablo has felt poorly for many days and is getting worse. What now?
o: Tell an adult so a doctor can check
Wait silently and hope it goes
Take some of his friend's medicine to feel better
questions.why: Getting worse is a reason to see a doctor.

questions.q: Match the word to its meaning.
pairs: Given to help, by a trusted adult
questions.why: These words describe being ill and getting better.

panel.q: Why can a doctor not just give medicine to everyone with a cough?
o: Different causes need different care, and medicine can be unsafe
Coughs are all exactly the same
Medicine always works the same way, so doctors save it for special days
panel.why: Doctors find the cause first and choose carefully.

panel.q: Ola says 'I will never tell anyone I am ill'. What is the problem?
o: Adults cannot help if they do not know
There is no problem at all
Illness always goes away faster if nobody knows
Doctors want to be told nothing
panel.why: Telling an adult gets help early.

panel.q: Why is rest important when you are ill?
panel.model: Resting lets your body save energy to fight the illness and mend.
panel.why: Rest helps recovery.

teach.topic: What to do when you feel ill
teach.model: When you feel ill, tell a grown-up. Rest and drink water. Only take medicine from a grown-up who knows. If you feel very bad or get worse, a doctor should check.

points.ask: When should a doctor see me?
